questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to breathe correctly when exercising in the gym
The history of Buddhism and how it spread to the West
Mindfulness becoming popular, especially in schools
Why children find it hard to concentrate in class
questions.why: Neil says they're exploring the rise of mindfulness, particularly in schools.

questions.q: How does Catherine react when Neil asks her to close her eyes and focus on her breathing?
options: She asks to do it later because time is short
She does it straight away
She laughs and refuses
She says she already did it this morning
questions.why: Catherine says, 'Can we do this later? We've only got six minutes.'

questions.q: What does Neil say about where mindfulness is used?
options: It is only practised in temples and other religious places
It is mainly used in hospitals to help patients with pain
It is becoming less popular now that people are busier
It began in Buddhism but is now used in non-religious places
questions.why: He says it's traditionally linked with Buddhism and is now very popular in workplaces, classes and schools.

questions.q: Why does teacher Alison Mayo think mindfulness suits young children?
options: They enjoy sitting still
It is natural for them to live in the present
They have more free time than adults
Their parents ask for it
questions.why: She says, 'That's very natural for children – to be in the present.'

questions.q: According to Alison Mayo, when does learning happen more easily?
options: When children are relaxed and happy
When children are a little stressed
When lessons are very short
When children work alone
questions.why: She says 'learning happens so much more easily if you're relaxed and happy'.

questions.q: Which of these benefits of mindfulness is NOT mentioned?
options: It may help treat depression and anxiety
It lowers levels of a stress hormone
It improves children's exam results
Eating mindfully may help people lose weight
questions.why: They mention depression and anxiety, cortisol and mindful eating, but not exam results.

questions.q: What criticism of the research on mindfulness is mentioned?
options: The studies are too old
Mostly only positive results get published
The studies only looked at children
Scientists were paid by schools
questions.why: Neil says critics point to a publication bias: only the positive results are published.

questions.q: How does Neil explain the difference between meditation and mindfulness?
options: They are exactly the same thing with two different names
Mindfulness is a religious practice, but meditation is not
Meditation is only for experts who have trained for years
Meditation is the wider term; mindfulness is one kind of it
questions.why: Neil says meditation is the broader term and mindfulness is a particular kind of meditation.
